s: The Constitution (Seventy-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992, popularly known as the Nagarpalika Act, came into force on which date?
x: The 74th Amendment came into force on 1 June 1993. 24 April 1993 is associated with the commencement of the 73rd Amendment.
tq: Use the close-date trap by distinguishing the commencement dates of the 73rd and 74th Amendments.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constitution (Seventy-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992:
1. It was passed by both Houses of Parliament in December 1992.
2. Presidential assent was given in April 1993.
3. It came into force on 24 April 1993.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the 74th Amendment came into force on 1 June 1993; 24 April 1993 was the commencement date of the 73rd Amendment.
tq: Separate the passage, assent and commencement dates instead of treating them as one event.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s: Which Part of the Constitution was inserted by the Constitution (Seventy-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992?
o: Part X relating to Scheduled and Tribal Areas
Part IXA relating to the Municipalities
x: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA, titled “The Municipalities”.
tq: Test the exact constitutional Part and its subject rather than the amendment number alone.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s: Part IXA of the Constitution, inserted by the 74th Amendment, extends from:
x: Part IXA, “The Municipalities”, comprises Articles 243P to 243ZG.
tq: Recall the precise constitutional article range and reject the nearby Part IX range.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s: The 74th Amendment inserted which of the following Schedules in the Constitution?
x: The 74th Amendment inserted the Twelfth Schedule, which contains 18 municipal functions linked to Article 243W.
tq: Use the amendment-to-Schedule association as a direct constitutional recall question.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the constitutional effect of the 74th Amendment?
o: It abolished the distinction among municipal corporations, municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.
It made local government a Union List subject and municipalities optional for all States.
It transferred all municipal taxation powers exclusively to the Union Government.
It gave urban local bodies constitutional status and made a uniform municipal framework obligatory for States.
x: The 74th Amendment gave urban local bodies constitutional status and required States to establish a uniform municipal framework through conforming laws.
tq: Choose the option that combines the two distinct consequences without adding an extreme claim.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to urban local government in India, consider the following statements:
1. Local Government continues to be a subject in the State List.
2. The 74th Amendment transferred Local Government to the Union List.
3. Municipal laws were required to be brought into conformity with the Constitution within one year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Local Government remains in the State List, and Article 243ZF required municipal laws to be brought into conformity within one year. Statement 2 is false because the subject was not transferred to the Union List.
tq: Identify the wrong-list trap and connect Article 243ZF with the one-year compliance requirement.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is a compulsory provision to be incorporated in State municipal law under the 74th Amendment?
o: The manner of electing the Mayor
Direct election of all members from wards
Representation of Members of Parliament in municipalities
x: Direct election of all municipal members from wards is compulsory. Representation of MPs, reservation for backward classes and the manner of electing the Chairperson are left to State legislatures.
tq: Distinguish mandatory constitutional requirements from provisions left to State legislative choice.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT a compulsory provision under the 74th Amendment?
o: Reservation for backward classes in every municipality
Ward Committees in municipalities having a population of three lakh or more
Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to population
x: Reservation for backward classes is voluntary and is left to the State legislature. Ward Committees for municipalities with a population of three lakh or more, five-year terms, and SC/ST reservation are compulsory provisions.
tq: Find the provision expressly left to State legislative discretion among otherwise mandatory features.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Article)
(a) Article 243Q
(b) Article 243R
(c) Article 243S
(d) Article 243T

List-II (Provision)
(i) Ward Committees
(ii) Reservation of seats
(iii) Types of municipalities
(iv) Composition of municipalities
x: Article 243Q deals with types of municipalities, Article 243R with their composition, Article 243S with Ward Committees and Article 243T with reservation of seats.
tq: Start with the sure Article–subject pairs and eliminate codes that reverse adjacent provisions.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s: A municipality has a population of 3 lakh. Which constitutional requirement becomes applicable to it under the 74th Amendment?
o: The Mayor must be directly elected by all residents of the State.
A Ward Committee must be constituted.
The municipality must be converted into a Municipal Corporation.
Reservation for backward classes becomes compulsory.
x: Ward Committees are compulsory in municipalities having a population of three lakh or more. The other consequences do not automatically follow from the population threshold.
tq: Apply the population threshold in Article 243S to a concrete municipal situation.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding municipal tenure and elections:
1. A municipality has a five-year term.
2. An election must be held within six months of dissolution of a municipality.
3. The State Election Commission is responsible for municipal elections.
4. The State Finance Commission reviews the financial position of municipalities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct. Articles 243U, 243ZA and 243Y provide the relevant constitutional framework for tenure, elections and financial review.
tq: Recognize a complete cluster of related compulsory provisions and select the comprehensive combination.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following matters is voluntary and may be decided by the State legislature under the 74th Amendment?
o: The five-year term of a municipality
The manner of electing the municipal Chairperson
Ward Committees in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more
State Election Commission supervision of municipal elections
x: The manner of electing the Chairperson or Mayor is left to the State legislature. The other three are compulsory constitutional provisions.
tq: Use the compulsory-versus-voluntary table to identify the discretionary provision.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

(a) Article 243W — Powers, authority and responsibilities of municipalities
(b) Article 243X — State Election Commission
(c) Article 243Y — Ward Committees
(d) Article 243ZF — Reservation of seats
x: Article 243W concerns municipal powers, authority and responsibilities, including Twelfth Schedule subjects. Articles 243X, 243Y, 243ZF respectively concern municipal taxation and funds, the State Finance Commission, and conformity of existing laws.
tq: Check the constitutional article attached to each provision and reject swapped article numbers.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s: The Twelfth Schedule contains how many functional items relating to municipalities?
x: The Twelfth Schedule contains 18 municipal functional items. The Eleventh Schedule, relating to Panchayats, contains 29 subjects.
tq: Distinguish the numerical count of the Twelfth Schedule from the larger Eleventh Schedule count.
sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is included in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals
x: Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals are Twelfth Schedule subjects. Non-conventional energy, small-scale industries and technical and vocational education are Eleventh Schedule subjects used as distractors.
tq: Separate municipal Twelfth Schedule functions from Panchayat Eleventh Schedule distractors.
sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT a subject in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries
x: Libraries and markets and fairs are listed under the Eleventh Schedule, not the Twelfth Schedule. Urban poverty alleviation, urban forestry and environmental protection, and regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries are Twelfth Schedule subjects.
tq: Use the municipal-versus-Panchayat list distinction to identify the excluded subject.
sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Twelfth Schedule subject)
(a) Urban and town planning
(b) Water supply
(c) Fire services
(d) Urban poverty alleviation

List-II (Functional group)
(i) Social
(ii) Infrastructure
(iii) Planning
(iv) Infrastructure
x: Urban and town planning belongs to the Planning group; water supply and fire services are Infrastructure subjects; urban poverty alleviation belongs to the Social group.
tq: Begin with the distinctive planning and social pairs, then resolve the two infrastructure entries.
sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Regulation of land use and building construction — Planning
2. Roads and bridges — Infrastructure
3. Public health, sanitation and solid waste management — Health and environment
4. Slum improvement and upgradation — Social
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: All four pairs are correctly matched with the functional groups of the Twelfth Schedule.
tq: Verify each pair against the functional classification rather than relying on a single familiar subject.
sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following sets consists entirely of Twelfth Schedule subjects relating to amenities and culture?
1. Parks, gardens and playgrounds
2. Cultural, educational and aesthetic aspects
3. Street lighting, parking, bus stops and public conveniences
4. Technical and vocational education
x: Items 1, 2 and 3 are Twelfth Schedule municipal subjects. Technical and vocational education is an Eleventh Schedule subject and is therefore excluded.
tq: Spot the single Panchayat-list insertion into an otherwise municipal group.
sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Regulatory group of the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Vital statistics, including registration of births and deaths
x: Vital statistics, including births and deaths, are included in the Regulatory group. Urban poverty alleviation is a Social subject, urban forestry belongs to Health and environment, and parks and gardens belong to Amenities and culture.
tq: Discriminate among closely related functional groups by matching the exact municipal responsibility.
sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

s:
Which one of the following combinations contains only subjects found in the Eleventh Schedule and NOT in the Twelfth Schedule?
1. Non-conventional energy
2. Small-scale industries
3. Technical and vocational education
4. Public amenities such as street lighting and parking
x: Non-conventional energy, small-scale industries and technical and vocational education are Eleventh Schedule subjects. Street lighting and parking are Twelfth Schedule municipal amenities.
tq: Use elimination by separating the three Panchayat subjects from the municipal amenity.
sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

s:
Assertion (A): The Twelfth Schedule includes functions relating to urban poverty alleviation.
Reason (R): The Twelfth Schedule is concerned exclusively with physical infrastructure such as roads, bridges and water supply.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: The Assertion is true because urban poverty alleviation is a Twelfth Schedule subject. The Reason is false because the Schedule also covers social, environmental, cultural and regulatory functions, not exclusively physical infrastructure.
tq: Test the absolute word “exclusively” in the Reason against the wider range of municipal functions.
sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is an environmental function included in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Promotion of non-conventional energy in rural areas
Distribution under the Public Distribution System
Urban forestry and protection of the environment and ecology
x: Urban forestry and protection of the environment and ecology are included in the Twelfth Schedule. The other options are associated with Eleventh Schedule Panchayat subjects or related rural functions.
tq: Apply the urban qualifier to distinguish the Twelfth Schedule environmental function from rural-list distractors.
sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
(a) Fire services — Infrastructure
(b) Safeguarding weaker sections, including persons with disabilities — Social
(c) Vital statistics — Regulatory
(d) Slaughter houses and tanneries — Amenities and culture
x: Slaughter houses and tanneries belong to the Regulatory group, not Amenities and culture. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
tq: Check the functional category of the final item rather than accepting a familiar municipal activity at face value.
sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following constitutional developments in chronological order:
A. Commencement of the 73rd Amendment
B. Passage of the 74th Amendment by both Houses
C. Presidential assent to the 74th Amendment
D. Commencement of the 74th Amendment
x: The 74th Amendment was passed in December 1992, the 73rd Amendment commenced on 24 April 1993, Presidential assent to the 74th Amendment was given in April 1993, and the 74th Amendment commenced on 1 June 1993.
tq: Place the two commencement dates around the passage and assent events before fixing the final sequence.
sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

s: The District Planning Committee is constitutionally provided under which Article of the Constitution of India?
x: The District Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZD. Article 243ZE relates to the Metropolitan Planning Committee.
tq: Discriminate between the two closely related constitutional provisions.
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to the Metropolitan Planning Committee, consider the following statements:
1. It is constituted for every metropolitan area having a population of ten lakh or more.
2. Its constitutional provision is contained in Article 243ZE.
3. A metropolitan area may extend across more than one district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. An MPC is mandatory for a metropolitan area with a population of ten lakh or more, is provided under Article 243ZE, and such an area may span more than one district.
tq: Use the population threshold and Article number to eliminate partial combinations.
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal function of a Metropolitan Planning Committee?
o: To consolidate only the plans of district panchayats into a state plan
To prepare a draft development plan for the metropolitan area as a whole
To conduct elections to municipalities and panchayats
To prepare the annual budget of every municipality in the metropolitan area
x: The Metropolitan Planning Committee prepares a draft development plan for the whole metropolitan area. It is not an electoral or municipal budgeting body.
tq: Identify the institution by its precise planning function.
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of a Metropolitan Planning Committee:
1. Not less than two-thirds of its members are elected.
2. The elected members are chosen by and from among elected members of municipalities and chairpersons of panchayats in the area.
3. The elected representation is in proportion to the population of urban and rural areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. At least two-thirds of MPC members are elected from the specified municipal and panchayat representatives, with representation based on the urban-rural population ratio.
tq: Check composition, source of election and proportional representation separately.
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT a matter specifically associated with the draft plan considered by the District Planning Committee?
o: Appointment of the State Election Commissioner
Sharing of water and other resources
x: The DPC considers matters such as spatial planning, resource sharing, integrated infrastructure and environmental issues. Appointment of the State Election Commissioner is unrelated to its planning function.
tq: Find the institutional function that does not belong to the planning mandate.
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s:
Assertion (A): The District Planning Committee is not composed entirely of elected members.
Reason (R): The Constitution requires not less than four-fifths of its members to be elected, while the remaining composition is determined according to State law.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true, and the constitutional requirement of at least four-fifths elected members directly explains why the remaining members need not be elected.
tq: Test the trap that converts “not less than four-fifths” into “all members.”
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s: The elected members of a District Planning Committee are selected by and from among the elected members of which bodies?
o: Gram Panchayats and Panchayat Samitis only
x: The elected members of a DPC are chosen by and from among the elected members of the district panchayat and municipalities in the district.
tq: Identify the exact constituent institutions rather than nearby local bodies.
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the plans of the District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee is correct?
o: The DPC consolidates the plans of panchayats and municipalities into a draft district development plan, whereas the MPC prepares a draft plan for the metropolitan area as a whole.
The DPC prepares a draft plan for the whole metropolitan area, whereas the MPC prepares a district plan.
Both committees prepare plans exclusively for rural areas.
Neither committee is concerned with local plans.
x: The DPC consolidates panchayat and municipal plans into a district development plan. The MPC prepares a draft development plan covering the entire metropolitan area.
tq: Split the options by matching each committee with its planning area.
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s: Who forwards the draft plan prepared by the District Planning Committee or Metropolitan Planning Committee to the State Government?
o: The Chief Secretary in every case
The chairperson of the concerned committee
x: The chairperson of the concerned DPC or MPC forwards the draft plan to the State Government. The manner of choosing the chairperson is determined by State law.
tq: Use the “who performs this function?” method to avoid assigning the power to a constitutional authority by default.
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s: The manner of choosing the chairperson of a District Planning Committee and a Metropolitan Planning Committee is determined by:
o: The Constitution through a uniform national procedure
The Union Parliament through rules framed under Article 243ZD
The law made by the concerned State Legislature
x: State law determines the manner of choosing the chairperson of both the DPC and the MPC.
tq: Distinguish a constitutional framework from details left to State law.
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the DPC from the MPC?
1. The DPC is constituted at the district level, whereas the MPC is constituted for a metropolitan area.
2. The DPC requires not less than four-fifths elected members, whereas the MPC requires not less than two-thirds elected members.
3. The DPC is under Article 243ZD, whereas the MPC is under Article 243ZE.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements correctly distinguish the two committees with respect to area, elected share and constitutional Article.
tq: Compare the two institutions across area, composition and Article rather than relying on one feature.
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s: The constitutional provisions relating to District Planning Committees and Metropolitan Planning Committees were inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: DPCs and MPCs are part of Part IXA and were inserted through the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992. The 73rd Amendment concerns Panchayats under Part IX.
tq: Discriminate between the 73rd rural-local-body Amendment and the 74th urban-local-body Amendment.
sec: District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Municipal Corporations of Bombay and Calcutta were established.
B. Lord Mayo’s resolution on financial decentralisation.
C. Lord Ripon’s resolution on local self-government.
D. The first Municipal Corporation was established at Madras.
x: The correct sequence is Madras Corporation in 1688, Bombay and Calcutta Corporations in 1726, Lord Mayo’s resolution in 1870, and Lord Ripon’s resolution in 1882.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest milestones first, then place the intervening dates.
sec: FIRST Municipal Corporation - city and year, early municipalities  [APPSC]

s: The charter establishing the first Municipal Corporation in Madras was issued on:
x: The charter for the Madras Municipal Corporation was issued on 30 December 1687. The corporation began functioning on 29 September 1688.
tq: Separate the charter date from the date on which the corporation began functioning.
sec: FIRST Municipal Corporation - city and year, early municipalities  [APPSC]

s: The Municipal Corporations of Bombay and Calcutta were established in:
x: The Municipal Corporations of Bombay and Calcutta were established in 1726.
tq: Use the distinct early-municipality dates to distinguish 1726 from the later decentralisation milestones.
sec: FIRST Municipal Corporation - city and year, early municipalities  [APPSC]

s: The five KAVAL towns in which Uttar Pradesh set up corporations in 1953 were:
o: Kanpur, Agra, Bareilly, Allahabad and Lucknow
Kanpur, Aligarh, Varanasi, Agra and Lucknow
Kanpur, Agra, Varanasi, Allahabad and Lucknow
Kashi, Agra, Varanasi, Allahabad and Meerut
x: The five KAVAL towns were Kanpur, Agra, Varanasi, Allahabad and Lucknow. Uttar Pradesh set up corporations in these towns in 1953, followed by the UP Municipal Corporations Act, 1959.
tq: Expand the mnemonic by verifying every member of the named list.
sec: FIRST Municipal Corporation - city and year, early municipalities  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the constitutional history of urban local government?
1. The Municipalities Bill of 1989 lapsed.
2. P. V. Narasimha Rao’s Bill introduced in September 1991 became the 74th Constitutional Amendment.
3. The 74th Amendment incorporated urban local government provisions in Part IXA.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All three statements are correct. The 1989 Municipalities Bill lapsed, while the Bill introduced by P. V. Narasimha Rao in September 1991 resulted in the 74th Amendment and Part IXA.
tq: Trace the legislative sequence and identify the Amendment’s constitutional location.
sec: FIRST Municipal Corporation - city and year, early municipalities  [APPSC]

s: The head who presides over the council of a Municipal Corporation is generally known as the:
x: The Mayor, assisted by the Deputy Mayor, presides over the council of a Municipal Corporation. The Municipal Commissioner is its chief executive.
tq: Distinguish the elected presiding office from the appointed executive office.
sec: Functionaries → institution matching  [APPSC]

s: Who is the chief executive of a Municipal Corporation and is ordinarily appointed by the State Government?
x: The Municipal Commissioner is the chief executive of a Municipal Corporation and is appointed by the State Government, commonly from the IAS.
tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” method to separate political leadership from administration.
sec: Functionaries → institution matching  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Sarpanch — Gram Panchayat
2. Chairman or Chairperson — Zilla Parishad
3. Mayor — Municipal Corporation
4. Municipal Commissioner — elected head of a Gram Panchayat
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Municipal Commissioner is the State-appointed chief executive of a Municipal Corporation, not the elected head of a Gram Panchayat.
tq: Find the wrong functionary–institution pairing by distinguishing rural and urban offices.
sec: Functionaries → institution matching  [APPSC]

s:
The office of Chairperson is associated with which of the following institutions?
1. Zilla Parishad
2. Municipal Council
3. Nagar Panchayat
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Chairman or Chairperson is the designation associated with the Zilla Parishad as well as the Municipal Council and Nagar Panchayat.
tq: Test whether one office designation is used across the listed local institutions.
sec: Functionaries → institution matching  [APPSC]

s: Under Part IXA of the Constitution, which Article contains the definitions relating to municipalities?
x: Article 243P contains the definitions for the purposes of Part IXA, while Article 243Q deals with the constitution of municipalities.
tq: Use precise Article–subject matching rather than relying on adjacent Article numbers.
sec: Part IXA - Articles 243P to 243ZG

s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the three types of municipalities specifically recognised under Article 243Q?
x: Article 243Q recognises Nagar Panchayats for transitional areas, Municipal Councils for smaller urban areas and Municipal Corporations for larger urban areas. Cantonment Boards are other forms of urban local bodies outside this classification.
tq: Find the one institution outside the constitutional three-fold classification.
sec: Part IXA - Articles 243P to 243ZG

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Article 243R — Composition of municipalities
2. Article 243T — Reservation of seats
3. Article 243U — Duration of municipalities
4. Article 243X — Audit of municipal accounts
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: Articles 243R, 243T and 243U concern composition, reservation and duration respectively. Article 243X concerns taxes and funds; audit is dealt with by Article 243Z.
tq: Split the options by checking the closely placed Articles 243X and 243Z.
sec: Part IXA - Articles 243P to 243ZG

s: Which Article provides for the powers, authority and responsibilities of municipalities, including matters in the Twelfth Schedule?
x: Article 243W deals with the powers, authority and responsibilities of municipalities and links them with the Twelfth Schedule.
tq: Test the Article by its functional subject instead of its numerical proximity.
sec: Part IXA - Articles 243P to 243ZG

s: The power of municipalities to impose taxes and the arrangements for municipal funds are dealt with under:
x: Article 243X deals with the power to impose taxes and the constitution of municipal funds.
tq: Distinguish the powers-and-functions provision from the taxation-and-funds provision.
sec: Part IXA - Articles 243P to 243ZG

s:
With reference to the constitutional provisions relating to municipalities, consider the following statements:
1. Article 243Y connects the State Finance Commission under Article 243-I with municipal finances.
2. Article 243Z deals with audit of municipal accounts.
3. Article 243ZA assigns municipal elections to the Election Commission of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because municipal elections are conducted by the State Election Commission under Article 243ZA, not by the Election Commission of India.
tq: The wrong-authority trap is used in the statement concerning municipal elections.
sec: Part IXA - Articles 243P to 243ZG

s: Which of the following correctly describes Articles 243ZF and 243ZG?
o: They concern municipal taxation and audit respectively.
They concern reservation and duration of municipalities respectively.
They concern Union Territories and exempted areas respectively.
They concern existing laws and the bar on interference by courts in electoral matters respectively.
x: Article 243ZF deals with the continuance of existing laws for a specified period, while Article 243ZG bars court interference in electoral matters relating to municipalities.
tq: Use the distinctive end provisions of Part IXA to eliminate neighbouring subjects.
sec: Part IXA - Articles 243P to 243ZG

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the territorial application of Part IXA:
1. Article 243ZB deals with application to Union Territories.
2. Article 243ZC provides for exceptions relating to Scheduled and tribal areas.
3. The Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council is included among the areas to which these provisions automatically apply without exception.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Articles 243ZB and 243ZC deal with Union Territories and exempted areas respectively. The Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council is among the specifically mentioned exceptions, so statement 3 is false.
tq: Watch for the reversed application-and-exemption statement.
sec: Part IXA - Articles 243P to 243ZG

s: A municipality has been dissolved before completing its normal term. Under Article 243U, the election to reconstitute it should ordinarily be completed:
o: Only after the next general election
x: A municipal election must be held before expiry of the five-year term or, in the case of dissolution, within six months of dissolution, subject to the constitutional qualification relating to the remaining period.
tq: Apply the six-month rule to a dissolution scenario.
sec: Term, SEC and SFC for municipalities  [other exams, GROUP-II]

s: The term of a municipality under Article 243U is calculated from the date of its:
x: A municipality continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier according to law.
tq: Distinguish the constitutional starting point from election and notification dates.
sec: Term, SEC and SFC for municipalities  [other exams, GROUP-II]

s: Before a municipality is dissolved, which procedural safeguard is specifically associated with Article 243U?
o: The municipality must first complete two full terms.
The Governor must obtain the consent of the Union Cabinet.
The municipality must be heard before dissolution.
The State Election Commission must approve the dissolution unanimously.
x: The municipality must be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard before dissolution.
tq: Identify the procedural safeguard rather than the authority alleged to approve dissolution.
sec: Term, SEC and SFC for municipalities  [other exams, GROUP-II]

s: A person aged 22 years is otherwise eligible to contest a municipal election. Which statement is correct?
o: The person is ineligible because the minimum age is 25 years.
The person is eligible only if aged 30 years or more.
The person cannot contest municipal elections because Article 243V fixes no minimum age.
The person is eligible on the age criterion because the minimum age is 21 years.
x: Article 243V requires a minimum age of 21 years for municipal membership, not 25 years.
tq: Use the confusable 21-versus-25 age distinction.
sec: Qualifications to contest (Article 243V)  [other exams, GROUP-II]

s: Under Article 243V, disqualifications for membership of a municipality are determined primarily with reference to:
o: Only rules framed by the Union Government
The law made by the municipal council itself
Only the Representation of the People Act, 1951
The law applicable to elections to the State Legislature or a State law
x: A person may be disqualified under the law applicable to elections to the State Legislature or under a law made by the State Legislature.
tq: Identify the correct level of law governing disqualification.
sec: Membership - minimum age, disqualifications, SEC role  [other exams]

s: Which authority is responsible for electoral rolls and all municipal elections under Article 243ZA?
x: Article 243ZA places the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of municipal elections under the State Election Commission, the same constitutional authority associated with Article 243K.
tq: Ask who would do this job and reject the similarly named Union body.

s: In the clarification concerning ex-officio voting in mayoral elections in Telangana, which persons were stated to be eligible to vote when registered as electors in the concerned urban local body?
